tui.settings_view.chrome.capture.contrac.note: Key contract while a shortcut row is listening. {cancel_key} ('esc') is a key name inserted verbatim.
Key contract once a shortcut has been captured but not yet saved. {save_key} ('enter') and {cancel_key} ('esc') are key names inserted verbatim.

tui.settings_view.chrome.capture.listeni.note: Detail line while a shortcut row waits for the user to press the key to bind.

tui.settings_view.chrome.capture.press_a.note: Detail line while a shortcut row is listening and the pressed key was refused (reserved or not capturable): asks the user to press a different key.

tui.settings_view.chrome.capture.saved.note: Detail-line notice after a captured shortcut was written. {shortcut} is the shortcut as displayed (e.g. 'ctrl+k'), inserted verbatim.

tui.settings_view.chrome.capture.takes_f.note: Shown while a captured shortcut is pending when that key is already bound to another action: confirming steals it. {shortcut} is the shortcut (e.g. 'ctrl+k'); {victim} is the name of the action losing it. Keep the quotation marks around {victim} (use the locale's own quotation marks).

tui.settings_view.chrome.cascade.cleared.note: Detail-line notice after the user pressed r on a corrupt fallback cascade and it was deleted. The settings page's detail line is about 74 cells at 80 columns.

tui.settings_view.chrome.cascade.empty.note: Indented row under the fallback-cascade setting when no failover chains exist.

tui.settings_view.chrome.cascade.expecte.note: Detail-line error when the user submits an empty new-chain line. {syntax} is the literal input shape '<chain-key> <provider>/<model>' inserted verbatim.

tui.settings_view.chrome.cascade.first_h.note: Detail-line error when a new chain's first hop (provider/model) is invalid. {problem} is the validator's own explanation, inserted as-is. A hop is one provider/model step in a failover chain.

tui.settings_view.chrome.cascade.malform.note: Indented row under the fallback-cascade setting when the stored value is corrupt (not a mapping). {key} is the key name 'r' inserted verbatim; pressing it deletes the corrupt value.

tui.settings_view.chrome.cascade.reset_r.note: Detail-line notice when r is pressed on a healthy fallback cascade: r does not reset the whole cascade; chains are deleted one at a time with d on the chain's own row. {reset_key} ('r') and {delete_key} ('d') are key names inserted verbatim.

tui.settings_view.chrome.clause.default.note: Detail-line clause on a setting changed from its default, naming the default value. {value} is the value as the page displays it.

tui.settings_view.chrome.clause.inert.note: Detail-line clause on a setting whose master switch is off, so it currently has no effect. {master} is the master setting's label.

tui.settings_view.chrome.clause.no_limit.note: Detail-line clause on the session-cleanup master switch when it is on but no cleanup limits are set in the rows below it.

tui.settings_view.chrome.clause.not_save.note: Detail-line clause while a list of choices is expanded: nothing is written until {save_key} ('enter', a key name inserted verbatim) is pressed.

tui.settings_view.chrome.clause.would_re.note: Detail-line clause on the session-cleanup master switch: how many stored sessions the configured policy would delete at the next launch. {count} selects the plural; {shown} is the same number as raw digits. {command} is the literal CLI command 'lop sessions cleanup --dry-run' inserted verbatim.

tui.settings_view.chrome.confirm.ask.note: Detail-line question before deleting a failover chain. {chain} is the user's chain name (may be cropped with …); {count} selects the plural, {shown} is the same number as raw digits. A hop is one provider/model step in the chain. Followed on the same line by the key contract.

tui.settings_view.chrome.confirm.contrac.note: Key contract after the delete-chain question. {key} ('d') and {cancel_key} ('esc') are key names inserted verbatim. Sheds to the short form when the chain name would be cropped.
Narrow form of the delete-chain key contract. {key} ('d') and {cancel_key} ('esc') are key names inserted verbatim.

tui.settings_view.chrome.error.config_un.note: Detail-line error when the config file cannot be parsed, so a save was refused. {file} is the file name 'config.yml' inserted verbatim; {error} is the parser's own message.

tui.settings_view.chrome.error.not_text.note: Detail-line message when a setting kind has no text editor.

tui.settings_view.chrome.error.retired.note: Detail-line message when enter is pressed on a read-only, retired setting.

tui.settings_view.chrome.error.save_fail.note: Detail-line error for any other failed write (read-only directory, full disk). {error} is the system's message.

tui.settings_view.chrome.error.unexpecte.note: Detail-line error when the config file parses but holds the wrong shape underneath. {path} is the config file's path; {error} is the original technical message, kept for bug reports.

tui.settings_view.chrome.footer.any_key.note: Footer key-hint label painted right after a key glyph in the settings page's bottom hint bar (e.g. '↑↓ move'); a single space separates them. The bar sheds whole hints right-to-left when the terminal is narrow, so keep it a short verb. Beside ↑↓ while the row is listening for a shortcut: any key pressed is captured (the arrows are not moving the cursor).

tui.settings_view.chrome.footer.back.note: Footer key-hint label painted right after a key glyph in the settings page's bottom hint bar (e.g. '↑↓ move'); a single space separates them. The bar sheds whole hints right-to-left when the terminal is narrow, so keep it a short verb. Beside esc, the narrow form of 'back to conversation': esc leaves the settings page.

tui.settings_view.chrome.footer.back_to_.note: Footer key-hint label painted right after a key glyph in the settings page's bottom hint bar (e.g. '↑↓ move'); a single space separates them. The bar sheds whole hints right-to-left when the terminal is narrow, so keep it a short verb. Beside esc when nothing is pending: esc leaves the settings page and returns to the chat transcript. Widest form; the bar falls back to the 'back' label when it does not fit.

tui.settings_view.chrome.footer.cancel.note: Footer key-hint label painted right after a key glyph in the settings page's bottom hint bar (e.g. '↑↓ move'); a single space separates them. The bar sheds whole hints right-to-left when the terminal is narrow, so keep it a short verb. Beside esc while editing, choosing, capturing or confirming a delete: esc cancels that and stays on the page.

tui.settings_view.chrome.footer.change.note: Footer key-hint label painted right after a key glyph in the settings page's bottom hint bar (e.g. '↑↓ move'); a single space separates them. The bar sheds whole hints right-to-left when the terminal is narrow, so keep it a short verb. Beside enter: enter opens/changes the selected setting.

tui.settings_view.chrome.footer.choose.note: Footer key-hint label painted right after a key glyph in the settings page's bottom hint bar (e.g. '↑↓ move'); a single space separates them. The bar sheds whole hints right-to-left when the terminal is narrow, so keep it a short verb. Beside enter while a list of choices is expanded: enter picks the highlighted choice.

tui.settings_view.chrome.footer.complete.note: Footer key-hint label painted right after a key glyph in the settings page's bottom hint bar (e.g. '↑↓ move'); a single space separates them. The bar sheds whole hints right-to-left when the terminal is narrow, so keep it a short verb. Beside tab while a suggestion dropdown is open: tab completes the highlighted suggestion into the field.

tui.settings_view.chrome.footer.confirm.note: Footer key-hint label painted right after a key glyph in the settings page's bottom hint bar (e.g. '↑↓ move'); a single space separates them. The bar sheds whole hints right-to-left when the terminal is narrow, so keep it a short verb. Beside enter while a captured shortcut is pending: enter commits it.

tui.settings_view.chrome.footer.default.note: Footer key-hint label painted right after a key glyph in the settings page's bottom hint bar (e.g. '↑↓ move'); a single space separates them. The bar sheds whole hints right-to-left when the terminal is narrow, so keep it a short verb. Beside r: r resets the selected setting to its default value. Imperative sense 'reset to default'.

tui.settings_view.chrome.footer.move.note: Footer key-hint label painted right after a key glyph in the settings page's bottom hint bar (e.g. '↑↓ move'); a single space separates them. The bar sheds whole hints right-to-left when the terminal is narrow, so keep it a short verb. Beside ↑↓: the arrow keys move the cursor between settings rows.

tui.settings_view.chrome.footer.move_can.note: Footer key-hint label painted right after a key glyph in the settings page's bottom hint bar (e.g. '↑↓ move'); a single space separates them. The bar sheds whole hints right-to-left when the terminal is narrow, so keep it a short verb. Beside ↑↓ while a text editor is open: moving off the row cancels the edit. Reads as the key's two effects (move, and that cancels), not a sentence.

tui.settings_view.chrome.footer.panes.note: Footer key-hint label painted right after a key glyph in the settings page's bottom hint bar (e.g. '↑↓ move'); a single space separates them. The bar sheds whole hints right-to-left when the terminal is narrow, so keep it a short verb. Beside ←→: left/right switch the read-only side pane between its teams and agents tabs.

tui.settings_view.chrome.footer.save.note: Footer key-hint label painted right after a key glyph in the settings page's bottom hint bar (e.g. '↑↓ move'); a single space separates them. The bar sheds whole hints right-to-left when the terminal is narrow, so keep it a short verb. Beside enter while editing a value: enter saves it.

tui.settings_view.chrome.footer.suggesti.note: Footer key-hint label painted right after a key glyph in the settings page's bottom hint bar (e.g. '↑↓ move'); a single space separates them. The bar sheds whole hints right-to-left when the terminal is narrow, so keep it a short verb. Beside ↑↓ while a suggestion dropdown is open: the arrows browse the suggestions.

tui.settings_view.chrome.gate_kept.long.note: Widest of three detail-line forms after an approvals setting was saved but this running session keeps its stricter gate. {command} is the literal command '/approvals auto' inserted verbatim. The line sheds to shorter forms when narrow; the command is the part that must survive.

tui.settings_view.chrome.gate_kept.mediu.note: Middle form of the gate-kept alert (see gate_kept.long). {command} is '/approvals auto' inserted verbatim.

tui.settings_view.chrome.gate_kept.short.note: Narrowest form of the gate-kept alert (see gate_kept.long). {command} is '/approvals auto' inserted verbatim.

tui.settings_view.chrome.hotkey.desktop_.note: Detail line for a desktop-app global shortcut row: the terminal can capture only keys it receives; any other chord is set in the desktop app.

tui.settings_view.chrome.hotkey.hold_det.note: Detail line for a desktop hold-to-talk shortcut row: a terminal cannot capture a held modifier, so it is set only in the desktop app.

tui.settings_view.chrome.hotkey.hold_ref.note: Detail-line refusal when enter is pressed on a hold-to-talk shortcut row in the terminal.

tui.settings_view.chrome.hotkey.recordin.note: Detail line for the desktop speech-to-text recording shortcut (delivered to the focused desktop window, not global). Must fit one line at 100x30.

tui.settings_view.chrome.notice.discarde.note: Detail-line notice after an edited value was abandoned: the typed text was not saved. Explains the editor's rule: {save_key} ('enter') saves, {cancel_key} ('esc') or moving the cursor away cancels. Key names inserted verbatim.

tui.settings_view.chrome.value.auto.note: Value column of a tri-state setting that is unset (e.g. display.nerd_icons): the program decides automatically. Matches the word `config edit` accepts in English, but here it is display only.

tui.settings_view.chrome.value.chains.note: Value column of the fallback-cascade setting: how many failover chains are configured. {count} selects the plural; {shown} is the same number as raw digits — insert {shown}, do not localise digits.
